## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Rewriting `requirement_proven` from `all()` to a `sum()` comparison drops the old `bool(criteria)` guard. A requirement with no criteria now counts as proven, and a criterion whose `proven` value is not a boolean or number now raises an error instead of evaluating as false. `reviewed_batch` is correct and well tested. The `REVIEW_HINT` constant is unused data and has no effect on behaviour.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — For `requirement_proven([])`, `proven` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so the function now returns `True`. Before this change, `bool(criteria) and ...` made it return `False`. The new test at tests/test_proof.py:6-8 never passes an empty list, so nothing catches this. Could you restore the emptiness check, e.g. `return bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and add `assert not requirement_proven([])`? — A requirement with no criteria at all is now reported as proven, which is the opposite of the old result and of the "requires entries" rule this PR applies in `reviewed_batch`.

## Important
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — `sum(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` needs every `proven` value to be numeric. A criterion that hasn't been evaluated yet, such as `{"proven": None}` (a common JSON null), raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'NoneType'`. Under the old `all()` it was simply falsy. A non-boolean truthy value like `{"proven": 2}` next to `{"proven": False}` also gives `2 == 2` and returns `True`. Could you go back to an `all()`-based truth test so each value is checked for truthiness and not added up? — Proof summaries crash on criteria that have no result yet, and they report proven when the values are counts rather than booleans.

## Strengths
- `reviewed_batch` rejects an empty batch with a clear `ValueError`. tests/test_proof.py:11-17 covers the empty, single-true, all-true, single-false and mixed cases.
